trades: who used to hold a sword

fetch.title: A ring in the reeds
fetch.text: It came off her hand at {place} the summer her husband died. She would like it back before she forgets which finger.

fetch.title: The good knife
fetch.text: Left at {place}. It is a perfectly ordinary knife. It is also the only one that cuts bread properly.

fetch.title: Blue flowers
fetch.text: They only grow at {place}, and only briefly. Bring an armful. Do not ask who they are for.

fetch.title: A name on a stone
fetch.text: There is a marker at {place}. Read what it says and bring the words back. I cannot make the walk any more.

fetch.title: My father's boots
fetch.text: He walked to {place} and did not walk back. The boots are worth more than the sentiment, but only just.

fetch.title: The other half
fetch.text: We broke a coin between us at {place} and each took a piece. He is dead. I would like the set.

deliver.title: A letter, unhurried
deliver.text: Take this to {place}. There is no rush. He has waited nine years; he can wait for you to arrive.

deliver.title: Seed for the spring
deliver.text: {place} lost their store to the rain. It will keep. Walk carefully with it.

deliver.title: Six coppers
deliver.text: A debt owed to a man in {place}. I have been meaning to send it since before you were born.

deliver.title: Word of a death
deliver.text: Someone in {place} should be told. Do not soften it. She will know if you do.

deliver.title: A jar of preserves
deliver.text: For my sister at {place}. She will say she did not want any. Leave it anyway.

cull.title: The wolves again
cull.text: {count} of them at least, and they have had the ewe already.

cull.title: Something in the field
cull.text: {count} {target}, near enough. Nobody will go out after dark now.

cull.title: Bad neighbours
cull.text: Clear out {count} {target}. They have been told once. They did not take it well.

cull.title: The road is not safe
cull.text: {count} {target} working the road. The carts have stopped coming and the price of everything has gone up.

cull.title: It comes back
cull.text: We drove them off last winter and the winter before. {count} {target}. We will be asking again next year.

look.title: See if it still stands
look.text: There was a tree at {place}. I planted it. Go and see whether it is still there, and come back and lie to me if it is not.

look.title: The flowers at {place}
look.text: They open once and they do not last. I have never been. Go and see them for me.

look.title: Where the field was
look.text: There was a battle at {place}, long enough ago that the grass has forgotten it. Stand there a while.

look.title: The view
look.text: From {place} you can see the whole valley. That is all. That is the whole errand.

look.title: The names we carved
look.text: My party cut their names into the rock at {place}. I am the last of them. See that it is still legible.

look.title: Sunrise, apparently
look.text: Someone told me the light comes up over {place} in a way worth walking for. I have never had the time.

seen: You stand a while at {place}. It is exactly as small as it was described.
{place}, and it is still there. Somebody will be glad, and somebody will pretend not to be.
There is nothing at {place} but the thing you were sent to look at. It was worth the walk.
You look at {place} for as long as it takes. Then you go on.
